lead: Delaware's small size hides a varied fire picture, from Wilmington rowhomes to propane-heated homes in Sussex County. SootMend helps homes and businesses statewide recover from fire, smoke and soot.
risk: kitchen and heating fires, rowhome fires, and propane and oil heat fires
why: About one in ten Delaware homes heats with propane and nearly 7% with fuel oil, more in rural Kent and Sussex counties. Puff-backs from oil burners and propane heater fires are common winter calls. Beach towns have many seasonal homes that sit empty for months.

Wilmington's rowhomes share walls and roofs, so a fire in one can damage the next. Delaware's fire death risk was about the national average in 2023, but USFA cautions that rates based on so few deaths vary.
problems: Smoke damage in empty beach homes
tips: Have oil and propane systems serviced every fall.
Ask a neighbor to check on seasonal homes during winter.
Install smoke alarms in every bedroom.
insurance: Seasonal beach homes may have vacancy limits, so read your policy and tell your insurer if a home is empty for long stretches.
areas: Wilmington, Dover, Newark, Middletown, Smyrna, Georgetown and the beach towns are all covered.

faq.q: Is smoke damage in a seasonal home covered if no one was there?
faq.a: Often, but some policies limit coverage when a home is vacant for a long time. Check the vacancy terms and report the loss as soon as you find it.
